title: GPU PCIe link flap cascade - field notes and runbook sketch
content:
Summary:

Rapid notes from a recurring on-call cluster where multiple GPU nodes experienced bursty correctable error counts and then a cascade of PCIe link retrains that correlate with driver micro-resets and transient kernel panics. Impact was 2–4 worker pods evicted per node over ~30m windows; user-facing latency increased for batch jobs with long sequences. This doc is a field journal + early runbook sketch; not final.

Why this is different from previous ECC/NVLink writeups:
- The dominant signal here is repeated PCIe link retrain negotiation and PHY retraining events on the host side (dmesg logs show pcie link down/up), often preceded by a short spike in fan tach oscillation and local PSU voltage transients.
- Driver resets are micro (gpu-reset cycle ~2s) and do not show the usual ECC surge profile. Instead we see a small burst of correctable errors followed by link re-negotiation and a re-enumeration of the device by the kernel.
- Affected nodes are mixed-workload hosts running long-lived model serving containers + periodic host-level GPU profiling jobs (perf/ptrace based). Suspected interaction: profiling probes + PCIe retrain flapping triggers firmware-side watchdog reset.

Observed impact (real):
- 2029-11-02 01:14 UTC: first spike - 3 pods evicted on node gnode-07 (ml-serving-tier). Job retries masked user-visible errors but increased 95th p99 latency by ~180ms on token production.
- 2029-11-02 03:22 UTC: cluster-wide correlated events across 6 nodes in rack-a3 within 8 minutes. Eviction cascades triggered autoscaler churn.
- Bulk telemetry: subtle rise in PCIe 'link down' events in last 72h window.

Human timeline (what oncall did):
- Triage: captured dmesg and driver logs from affected nodes (nvidia: gpu-reset messages, pcie: link down/up). Collected nv-hostengine logs and SRI telemetry.
- Immediate mitigation: cordon node + warm-migrate low-priority pods. For high-traffic nodes, switched to fallback model variant (smaller memory footprint) to reduce host memory pressure.
- Short-term fix: Disabled nightly profiling cron on affected hosts and paused hardware perf counters for 48h as an experiment.

Key evidence and signals we correlated:
- dmesg: repeated messages "pcie_bus 0000:65:00.0: PCIe link down" followed by "nvkm: GPU reset completed" and then a kernel driver rebind event.
- ipmitool / host sensor logs: short-lived spike in 12V line variance preceding first link retrain in 5/7 samples.
- fan tach: correlated 10–15% oscillation in PWM reported RPMs prior to first reset in some nodes.
- workload correlation: nodes running host-level perf sampling or ptrace-driven probes had 3x higher event probability.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Firmware/BIOS PCIe PHY micro-timing regression interacting with newer driver power management (autosuspend / ASPM) during high sampling workloads.
2) Host perf/probing toggles a register that nudges the GPU into a low-power lane, race with firmware link training results in flapping.
3) PSU ripple under particular thermal/fan regimes causes momentary link retrain; driver handles this with a reset but kernel state gets inconsistent leading to evictions.
4) Rare HW silicon flake in specific lot number of GPUs (less likely since multiple SKUs affected).

Triage checklist (concrete steps for next oncall):
- Immediately: capture full dmesg (sudo journalctl -k -b -1), /var/log/messages, and /var/log/nvidia-uvm.log. Save to /tmp/si-capture-<node>-YYYYMMDD.tgz.
- Check ipmi sensor values for 12V, 3.3V rails in the minute window before first link down.
- Pull kernel tracepoint around pcie: trace-cmd record -e pcie_link_status -e pci_hotplug -e nvidia_reset --sleep 30s (if safe).
- If link down count > 3 in 10m: cordon node, migrate long-running serving containers to standby pool.
- Disable host profiling cron and any perf/ptrace jobs; probe again for 2h.
- If resets continue after performance cron disabled: escalate to hardware (-hw) for rack-level power rail inspection; request PSU swap on node.

Runbook sketch for automation (minimal safe automations):
- Monitor rule: create alert when PCIe link_down events per node > 5 within 30m AND node eviction rate > 1 per 5m. Alert to #sre-pager.
- Automated mitigation: after alert, mark node "ephemeral-standby" and drain non-critical pods, set node kernel to keep driver bound (do not kill containerd right away).
- Auto-twist: if fan-tach oscillation correlates (rpm variance > 12% in 2m), trigger soft-thermal-profile that raises fan to 75% for 5m and force platform to ignore autosuspend for GPU devices (echo -n on > /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:65:00.0/power/control) for short window.
- Rollback: if automations cause higher impact, disable by feature-flag. Keep a manual override in SRE console.

Telemetry and data we need to add (short term):
- Increase sampling for pcie_link_up/down counters to 10s granularity for affected racks for 72h.
- Surface fan RPM variance, 12V rail voltage, and perf-host toggles next to GPU evictions in console so incidents show cross-signal correlation.
- Add per-node flag indicating whether host-level profiling is scheduled and when last run.

Experiment plan (for next week):
- Controlled A/B on 8 nodes: group A (disable perf/prof jobs, force ASPM off), group B (leave in current state). Run for 72h and measure link-down rate + evictions.
- If group A far better, implement cluster-wide host-profile gating: only run heavy host sampling during maintenance windows and ensure ASPM off while sampling.
- Work with firmware vendor to reproduce link retrain sequence with perf probes attached; capture PHY-level negotiation logs if possible.

Longer-term engineering asks (tickets to open):
- GH-PR to add a flag in our node agent to temporarily disable device autosuspend and to capture ipmi-sensor-history on PCIe link events (GH-PR-4123).
- SRE-OPS: inventory nodes by motherboard/PSU lot and map against incident occurrences (JIRA-SI-9876).
- FW: create repro harness for link retrain under toggled perf counters.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is there a firmware update in the field that landed ~2029-10 with PCIe PHY microcode? Check host firmware change log.
- Could the profiler be attaching a debug page that nudges the device into a non-standard power domain? Need to inspect perf sampling startup sequence.
- Do we have a subtle interaction with our kernel upgrade (5.19->6.2) and a backported pcie hotplug patch? Cross-check kernel changelogs.

Quick references (logs to look for):
- /var/log/kern.log -> search for "PCIe link" or "pcie_bus.*link down"
- /var/log/nvidia-uvm.log and nvidia-smi -q output timestamps
- ipmitool sensor list --thresholds for minute window around event
- node-agent logs: /var/log/node-agent/agent.log for "perf-cron" or "profiler: start" messages

Immediate action items (who/what):
- Aisha: run A/B experiment setup for 8 nodes and collect baseline (due 2029-11-06).
- Ben: add temporary alert rule for link_down + eviction correlation (JIRA SI-9876).
- Lina: schedule hardware checks for rack-a3 PSUs and pull board part-ids for nodes that had >= 2 events.
- Ravi: open firmware repro ticket with vendor, attach sample trace and perf startup sequence.

Final note: this felt messy oncall — the short-term wins were disabling host-level profilers and temporarily raising fans; both reduced event frequency but did not fully eliminate it. Keep incident notes here, but next steps require a careful A/B and vendor repro.

-- end of notes (draft)
